subject: Post-demo: heuristic validation + fallback plan for structured output
messages:
From: Patricia Gomez <patricia.gomez@hightidehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Hightide Product <product@hightidehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: validation/fallbacks for JSON output

Thanks for the demo this morning — the team and I appreciated the clear perf numbers and the routing options. A few items came up on our end specific to structured output reliability that we'd like to lock down before the pilot.

Top priorities for us:
- Strong schema enforcement for diagnostic payloads (we need to reject invalid objects early).
- A clear retry/fallback plan when constrained decoding still produces malformed JSON.
- How embeddings + reranker will be included in the scoring pipeline without adding >150ms p90 latency.

Can you send a short plan that covers: what you would enforce client-side (SDK validation), server-side (constrained decoding + token filtering), and what graceful degradation looks like (structured fallback fields, partial results)? Also please attach any sample schema or checklist we can review.

Patricia
Principal PM, Hightide Health
patricia.gomez@hightidehealth.com

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Patricia Gomez <patricia.gomez@hightidehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2027 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: validation/fallbacks for JSON output

Hi Patricia — thanks for the clear summary. Below is a concise plan (so you can share with your eng/product teams) plus next steps. Attaching a first-pass schema (schema-proposal-v1.json) and a short validation checklist (validation-checklist.xlsx).

High-level approach (client + server split):
- Client-side (SDK): quick pre-flight checks (required keys, basic types, length limits) to catch obvious errors before hitting the network. SDK will return structured ValidationError objects with codes so callers can decide retry vs user fallback.
- Server-side (runtime): constrained decoding with schema-aware post-parse validation. If the model output fails schema validation, runtime attempts a single constrained re-run using stricter decoding params (lower temperature, top-k/top-p constraints, and explicit JSON markers). If that re-run still fails, apply the fallback policy (see below).
- Fallbacks / graceful degradation: return a partial result with an errors array and a "fallback_reason" field. We recommend the client treat partial results as usable for display, but not for automated billing/critical workflows.

Embedding + reranker integration:
- Option A (Recommended for pilot): async reranker step that is called post-generation. Generation returns quickly with a candidate list; reranker runs in parallel but does not block the initial UI. If reranker finishes within 150ms, we surface scored results; otherwise we show the initial ranked list and mark that scores are pending.
- Option B: Synchronous rerank with dedicated reserved qps if you opt into Redwood Dedicated — adds predictable latency but simplifies consistency.

Retry policy (summary):
1) SDK pre-flight validation fail -> surface error to app (no network request).
2) First model call -> parse & validate. If success, return.
3) If invalid, server triggers constrained re-run (single attempt) with stricter decoding -> parse & validate.
4) If still invalid -> return partial-with-errors + link to manual-review artifact stored in customer bucket (if configured).

Owners & next steps:
- Marissa: produce constrained-decoding param set + JSON markers doc (action: deliver by Thu 5/14).
- Dev: draft SDK pre-flight validation API and example snippets for service-account auth and routing policy (action: deliver by Fri 5/15).
- Logan: coordinate pilot SOW and draft canary plan (action: send draft SOW by Mon 5/17).

Patricia — can you confirm whether Hightide prefers synchronous rerank guaranteed or async-first for the pilot? Also, if you want a short call to walk through the schema-proposal and checklist, we can book 30m tomorrow.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Logan — captured. Quick technical notes on constrained decoding and validation that I expect to include in the doc I'm producing: (quoting your plan inline)

> "server triggers constrained re-run (single attempt) with stricter decoding"

Proposed parameters for constrained re-run (empirically tuned):
- temperature: 0.0–0.2
- top_p: 0.6
- top_k: 40
- presence_penalty / frequency_penalty: 0
- max_new_tokens: same as original request to avoid truncation-induced errors

Schema enforcement layers:
1) Token-level anchors: wrap JSON with explicit start/end markers and prompt scaffold that enforces a single JSON blob (e.g., "BEGIN_JSON" / "END_JSON").
2) Post-parse validation: fast JSON schema (draft-07 compatible) check on the parsed object. Use ajv on the client and server for parity.
3) Field-level sanitizers: for free-text fields, run short sanity checks (length, allowed chars); for numeric fields, coerce/round when safe. Mark coercions in the errors array.

Validation + retry patterns (short):
- If schema errors are minor (missing optional fields, type coercion possible) -> apply deterministic coercion in runtime and mark result as "coerced" with details.
- If errors indicate the decoder produced partial JSON (trailing commas, unclosed braces) -> do one constrained re-run with stricter anchors and then re-validate.
- If errors indicate hallucinated enum values -> run a targeted repair pass: re-prompt with allowed enum values and only ask for the problematic field (cheap token cost). Limit to single attempt.

I'll attach a param table and examples in the doc (will populate schema-proposal-v1.json with example enums). Marissa
Senior Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Adding implementation-level details and SDK snippets (high level) to make the pilot easy to stand up. Quoting Marissa where relevant.

SDK pre-flight validation (client):
- API: validatePayload(payload) -> returns {ok: bool, issues: [code]}
- Default rule set shipped with SDK (required/optional keys, types, max lengths). Customers can register custom validators.

Auth / routing notes:
- We recommend service-account key (JSON) for server-to-server pilot calls. Redwood supports short-lived JWTs if you prefer avoiding long-lived keys.
- Routing: request metadata (region, SLA tier) is passed as headers: X-RW-Region, X-RW-Policy. For Hightide pilot use X-RW-Region=us-west and policy=pilot-htd to ensure reserved qps.

Embedding + reranker integration (implementation):
- Pipeline: 1) generation -> 2) lightweight canonicalization -> 3) embed candidate text using real-time embedder -> 4) rerank via cosine similarity + small MLP.
- To keep p90 under 150ms: run canonicalization + embedding in parallel on a dedicated CPU threadpool, and use smaller embedding models for reranking (e.g., 3x smaller quantized model). If async is acceptable, return early and update when scores arrive.

Error artifacts and observability:
- When we return partial-with-errors, we can persist the raw model output and the failed validation artifact to your S3/GCS bucket (you control retention). We'll include a signed URL in the response.

Deliverables I'll upload: SDK snippet examples, auth guide, and a small integration checklist. ETA: Fri 5/15.

Dev Patel

- Rerank approach: let's start async-first for the pilot (we want to see how much value reranking adds before committing to reserved latency).
- Synchronous rerank: we'll evaluate in month-1 pilot review if scores are consistently within 120–150ms.
- Call: 30m tomorrow at 9am PT works for our eng + product (I'll send a calendar invite).

Please include the signed URL pattern for error artifacts in the checklist. I'll share the invite and attach our internal schema guidance for HIPAA-adjacent diagnostic payloads.

Thanks,
Patricia
